GUI_ACCOUNT_COOLDOWN_MAX_SECONDS: The longest a per-account cool-down grows to (default 300). Must not be less than `GUI_ACCOUNT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS`, or the backend does not start.
GUI_ACCOUNT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS: Seconds a user name is refused (429, a right password included) after it trips the per-account counter (default 60). Each repeat, after another `GUI_ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES` failures, is twice as long up to `GUI_ACCOUNT_COOLDOWN_MAX_SECONDS`. Kept short on purpose: anyone can make a name fail, so a long value would let an attacker keep a real person out. Must be 1 or more while the cool-down is on.
GUI_ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES: Per-account sign-in cool-down (`SEC-15.11b`): how many failed sign-ins of one user name, from any addresses together, inside `GUI_ACCOUNT_WINDOW_SECONDS` start a cool-down for that name (default 20). `0` switches the cool-down off. The older per-address counters are not affected. Unknown names count like real ones.
GUI_ACCOUNT_WINDOW_SECONDS: Seconds in which `GUI_ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES` failures of one user name must fall to start a cool-down (default 600); also how long a quiet name's counter takes to forget, with no sign-in able to reset it. Must be 1 or more while the cool-down is on.
GUI_ADMIN_MFA_REQUIRED: `true`: a local `admin` account without an enrolled one-time code can reach only the enrolment routes (every other route answers 403 `MFA_ENROLMENT_REQUIRED`, and the GUI sends the admin to Account security). Needs `GUI_TOTP_KEY` (the start fails without it). Users of the identity provider are not affected: their provider asks for the second factor. Default `false`.
GUI_ADMIN_PASSWORD: Password of the GUI's `admin` user, set at first start. Empty: a random one is generated and written to `GUI_INITIAL_PASSWORD_FILE`, never logged. Changing it later does not change an existing user: use the user admin page.
GUI_AUDIT_EXPORT_DIR: A directory: `python -m app.retention` first writes the audit rows it is about to delete there as JSON lines, and deletes only the rows written. Empty (the default): delete without exporting. See docs/RETENTION.md.
GUI_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS: Days to keep a row of the GUI BFF's audit log (`gui_audit_log`) when `python -m app.retention` runs (from cron, or `kubectl exec deploy/gui-bff` on Kubernetes). 0 (the default) keeps them all. See docs/RETENTION.md.
GUI_COOKIE_SECURE: `true` (default): the session cookie is marked Secure, so a browser sends it only over HTTPS (http://localhost counts). Set `false` only for plain-HTTP access by a non-localhost name, such as a lab VM by IP.
GUI_DATABASE_URL: SQLAlchemy URL of the GUI backend's own database (users, audit trail, the generated JWT key). SQLite file by default; with several GUI backend replicas point them all at one shared database.
GUI_HEALTH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: Seconds the GUI backend waits for each module's `/health`, `/ready` and `/version` before showing it as unreachable on the dashboard. Raise it on a slow network.

GUI_INITIAL_PASSWORD_FILE.description: File (mode 0600) the generated first `admin` password is written to when `GUI_ADMIN_PASSWORD` is unset. It holds a password but is a path, not a secret itself; read it once, then change the password.

GUI_JWT_ALGORITHM: Algorithm that signs the GUI session token: `HS256` (default) with the shared `GUI_JWT_SECRET`, exactly as before; `RS256` or `ES256` with the key pair in `GUI_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE`, public keys at `/.well-known/jwks.json`. A token whose header names another algorithm is refused. Changing it signs every user out. Any other value stops the start.

GUI_JWT_PREVIOUS_KEY_FILES.description: Comma-separated paths of PEM files (a public key is enough) holding the signing keys of earlier rotations. Under `RS256` / `ES256` a session signed with one of them still verifies, matched by its `kid`, and the public key is published at `/.well-known/jwks.json`; none of them ever signs. Remove a file to end the sessions of that key. Must match `GUI_JWT_ALGORITHM`; an unreadable file stops the start. Empty (default): none.

GUI_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE.description: Path of the PEM private key (unencrypted PKCS#8 or traditional; RSA of at least 2048 bits for `RS256`, EC P-256 for `ES256`) that signs the GUI session token. Needed with `GUI_JWT_ALGORITHM=RS256` or `ES256`, refused with `HS256`; mount it as a secret (the chart's `gui.jwtKeySecretRef`). No inline form. An unreadable or unusable file stops the start.

GUI_JWT_SECRET: Key that signs the GUI session tokens. Empty: the first backend instance generates one and stores it in `GUI_DATABASE_URL`, so replicas on one database agree. Changing it signs every user out.
GUI_LOCAL_LOGIN_ENABLED: `true` (default): the GUI backend accepts username/password sign-in (and the `/api/token` password grant for scripts). `false` turns both off so every operator signs in through OIDC; it needs `GUI_OIDC_ENABLED=true` (the start fails otherwise). Leave it `true` as the break-glass admin path unless the identity provider is the only way in by policy.
GUI_LOGIN_MODE: Who may use the password form: `both` (default) offers OIDC when it is configured and the local form; `oidc` refuses `POST /api/login` and the `/api/token` password grant for every account except a break-glass one, so the identity provider's MFA applies (needs `GUI_OIDC_ENABLED=true`, the start fails otherwise); `local` does not offer OIDC even when it is configured.
GUI_OIDC_ALLOW_HTTP: `true` accepts plain-http URLs for the issuer, the provider's endpoints and the redirect URI when the host is not localhost. Lab use only: the code exchange and the signing keys then travel unprotected. Default `false`.
GUI_OIDC_CLIENT_ID: The client id registered for the GUI at the OIDC provider; ID tokens must name it in `aud`.
GUI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET: The OIDC client's credential, when the client is confidential. Prefer `GUI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE`; setting both is an error. Empty with no file: a public client, protected by PKCE alone.
GUI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE: File holding the OIDC client's credential (a mounted Kubernetes or Docker secret); one trailing newline is removed. An unreadable file stops the start.
GUI_OIDC_DEFAULT_ROLE: Role for a signed-in user none of whose groups is in `GUI_OIDC_GROUP_ROLE_MAP`: `viewer`, `operator` or `admin`. Empty (default): such a user is refused.
GUI_OIDC_ENABLED: `true` turns on OIDC sign-in (authorization code with PKCE) next to the local login: the sign-in page then offers 'Sign in with <GUI_OIDC_PROVIDER_NAME>'. Default `false`. With it on, the issuer, client id, redirect URI and a group-to-role mapping (or a default role) must be set or the backend does not start.
GUI_OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM: Name of the ID-token claim that carries the user's groups or roles (default `groups`): a list, or a string split on spaces and commas. A dotted name reaches into an object, such as `realm_access.roles`.
GUI_OIDC_GROUP_ROLE_MAP: How provider groups become GUI roles: comma-separated `group=role` pairs, role one of `viewer`, `operator`, `admin`, for example `smo-admins=admin,smo-ops=operator,smo-viewers=viewer`. A user in several mapped groups gets the highest role. Evaluated at every sign-in.
GUI_OIDC_ISSUER: Issuer URL of the OIDC provider, e.g. `https://keycloak.example.com/realms/smo`. Discovery is read from `<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration`, and ID tokens must carry exactly this `iss`. Must be https (http only for localhost or with `GUI_OIDC_ALLOW_HTTP`).
GUI_OIDC_POST_LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URI: Where the provider sends the browser after the end-session (RP-initiated logout) page, when it offers one; must be registered at the provider. Empty: the parameter is not sent and the provider shows its own page.
GUI_OIDC_PROVIDER_NAME: Name shown on the sign-in button, 'Sign in with <name>' (default `SSO`).
GUI_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI: Public URL of the GUI backend's `/api/oidc/callback` as the browser reaches it (for example `https://gui.example.com/api/oidc/callback`), registered as a valid redirect URI at the provider. Must be an absolute https URL (http only for localhost or with `GUI_OIDC_ALLOW_HTTP`).
GUI_OIDC_SCOPES: Space-separated scopes requested at sign-in (default `openid profile email`); must include `openid`. Add `groups` (or the provider's own scope) if the provider only puts group membership in the ID token on request.
GUI_OIDC_SCOPE_CLAIM: GUI-5: the ID-token claim that holds a user's region/tenant scope (`{"regions": [...], "tenants": [...]}`), given to the user at every sign-in as the role is; a claim that breaks the rules refuses the sign-in (`invalid_scope`), none is an unscoped user. Empty (default): scopes are set by an admin on the Users tab.
GUI_OIDC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: Seconds the GUI backend waits for each call to the OIDC provider (discovery, signing keys, the code exchange); default 10. A slower provider makes the sign-in fail with 'could not be reached'.
GUI_OPERATOR_PASSWORD: Password of the demo `operator` user created at first start. Empty: no such user is created. Does not change an existing user.
GUI_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS: Seconds a GUI session lasts after sign-in (default 8 hours); the user must sign in again after it. Shorten it for shared consoles.
GUI_TOTP_ISSUER: Name an authenticator app shows for the one-time code of a GUI account (the issuer in the otpauth:// link). Default `SMO Operator Console`.
GUI_TOTP_KEY: Key (at least 32 characters, for example `openssl rand -base64 32`) that encrypts the one-time-code secrets of local GUI accounts in `gui_user_totp` and keys the hash of their recovery codes. Prefer `GUI_TOTP_KEY_FILE`; setting both is an error. Empty with no file: enrolment is refused and an account that is already enrolled cannot sign in. Changing it makes every stored secret unreadable: reset the users' codes (Admin > Users) and enrol again.
GUI_TOTP_KEY_FILE: File holding the one-time-code key (a mounted Kubernetes or Docker secret); one trailing newline is removed. An unreadable file stops the start.
GUI_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS: How many reverse proxies stand between a browser and the GUI backend (default 1: the console's nginx). The sign-in lockout and per-source throttle take the client's address from the entry that many places from the right of `X-Forwarded-For`, which the nearest proxy wrote; what a client put further left is ignored. Set 2 behind an ingress in front of the console; set 0 when clients reach the backend directly (the header is then not believed). A wrong value (too low behind a proxy) makes every client one source, and a source throttle then affects everyone.
GUI_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: Seconds the GUI backend waits for an answer from R1 Termination when it proxies a page's request (default 30). A longer call is shown as a gateway timeout.
GUI_VIEWER_PASSWORD: Password of the demo `viewer` (read-only) user created at first start. Empty: no such user is created. Does not change an existing user.
R1_URL: Address the GUI backend reaches R1 Termination at, for health probes, `/bootstrap` and every proxied page request (default `http://r1-termination:8000`).
